html:
The Crimean Khanate was the state of the Crimean Tatars, on the Crimean peninsula and the steppe north of the Black Sea, from 1441 to 1783. It is on the map from 1492 to 1600.

It broke away from the Golden Horde under Hacı I Giray, whose descendants ruled it for its whole life. From the 1470s it was a vassal of the Ottoman Empire, which held the coastal ports. The khans built their palace at Bakhchysarai.

The khanate was a terror to its northern neighbours. Its horsemen raided Poland-Lithuania and Russia for captives, who were sold through Crimean ports to the Ottoman lands. In 1571 the khan burned Moscow. The Nogai Horde on the steppe often rode with the Crimeans.

Russia slowly gained the upper hand, and Catherine the Great annexed the khanate in 1783. In 1944 Stalin ordered the deportation of the whole Crimean Tatar people.
